findings.passage: Many people in Wisconsin want to vote, and are eligible to vote, but have been dissuaded from doing so by our ID requirements, first implemented in 2016.
findings.note: Press release statement issued in his name on the day of the Assembly floor debate on the photo-ID constitutional amendment; he says the ID requirement keeps eligible people from voting. Posted by Urban Milwaukee from his office.

findings.passage: While you can technically get a no cost ID in Wisconsin, it’s still practically impossible for people who don’t have access to the proper documents, don’t understand the process, or can’t get where they need to obtain one.
findings.note: Same statement; he describes the free state ID as hard to obtain in practice.

findings.passage: Voter fraud is not a widespread problem in the State of Wisconsin and is so infrequent that it’s difficult to count.
findings.note: Same statement; he gives his view of how common voter fraud is and cites a figure from a research group.

findings.passage: “We are vehemently opposed to allowing gun shows at Milwaukee County facilities. Under state law, the County is unable to enforce common sense rules for gun shows at our own facilities, such as only allowing federally licensed firearm dealers, requiring private sellers to perform background checks, and imposing reasonable waiting periods.
findings.note: Joint statement issued by three county supervisors, Clancy among them, opposing a proposal to allow gun shows at a county facility. The release says 'released the following statement', so the words are shared by the three. Posted on Urban Milwaukee under his name as author. He was then a county supervisor, not yet in the Assembly.

findings.passage: “Supporters of this proposal claim that gun sales have occurred at this show for more than 20 years without incident. Yet without the ability to register or check buyers, that claim is completely unsubstantiated.
findings.note: Same joint statement by three county supervisors including Clancy: argues that without registration or buyer checks nothing shows whether guns sold at the show were used in crimes.
